+    #[test]
+    fn http_retryability_follows_construction_site() {
+        assert!(http("HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: slow down", true).is_retryable());
+        assert!(http("connection reset by peer", true).is_retryable());
+        assert!(!http("HTTP 401 Unauthorized: bad key", false).is_retryable());
+        assert!(!http("request cancelled", false).is_retryable());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn cli_transient_phrasings_are_retryable_everything_else_final() {
+        assert!(cli("subprocess exited with 1: API Error: rate limit reached").is_retryable());
+        assert!(cli("Overloaded — please retry shortly").is_retryable());
+        assert!(cli("request timed out after 60s").is_retryable());
+        assert!(!cli("subprocess exited with 1: invalid api key").is_retryable());
+        assert!(!cli("unknown flag --frobnicate").is_retryable());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn config_and_credential_errors_are_fatal() {
+        for err in [

+            ProviderError::InvalidConfig("bad".to_string()),
+        ] {
+            assert!(!err.is_retryable());
+            assert!(err.is_fatal());
+        }

+#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
+async fn transient_provider_error_retries_once_and_run_completes() {
+    let _gate = env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_dr-gate");
+    let temp = repo_tempdir();
+    let server = MockServer::start(transient_then_success_script()).await;
+    write_config(temp.path(), &server.base_url());
+
+    let output = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_deadreckon"))
+        .arg("run")
+        .arg("--fresh")
+        .arg("--yes")
+        .arg("mock transient retry task")
+        .arg("--provider")
+        .arg("mock")
+        .arg("--sandbox")
+        .arg("none")
+        .arg("--max-spend")
+        .arg("1")
+        .arg("--no-docs")
+        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", temp.path().join("home"))
+        .output()
+        .expect("run deadreckon");
+    assert!(
+        output.status.success(),
+        "{}{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).contains("completed run"));
+
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
+    let run = list_runs(&paths, None)
+        .expect("runs")
+        .into_iter()
+        .next()
+        .expect("run");
+    let state = load_run(&paths, &run.run_id).expect("state");
+    assert_eq!(state.status, RunStatus::Completed);
+    // The retry is part of the audit trail, not a silent recovery.
+    let events = fs::read_to_string(state.run_root.join("events.jsonl")).expect("events");
+    assert!(
+        events.contains("transient provider error; retrying once"),
+        "{events}"
+    );
+    assert!(events.contains("retry succeeded; continuing"), "{events}");
+    // The failed attempt plus the full script: every fixture was consumed.
+    assert!(server.journal().len() >= 6, "{}", server.journal().len());
+}
+

295	    const MAX: usize = 240;
296	    if body.len() <= MAX {

299	    // Cut on a char boundary: error bodies can carry multibyte text, and a
300	    // byte slice would panic exactly while reporting a provider failure.
301	    let cut = (0..=MAX).rev().find(|i| body.is_char_boundary(*i)).unwrap_or(0);

303	}

125	    fn from_config_with_model_and_registry(
126	        config: ProviderConfigFile,
127	        override_provider: Option<&str>,
128	        override_model: Option<&str>,
129	        registry: &ProviderRegistry,
130	        catalog_override: Option<&ModelCatalogOverride>,
131	    ) -> Result<Self> {
132	        let mut providers = provider_entries_from_registry(registry);
133	        for (name, entry) in config.providers {
134	            if let Some(base) = providers.get_mut(&name) {
135	                merge_provider_entry(base, entry);
136	            } else {
137	                providers.insert(name, entry);
138	            }
139	        }
140	
141	        let route_names = if let Some(provider) = override_provider {
142	            vec![provider.to_string()]
143	        } else {
144	            configured_route_names(config.default_provider, config.fallback)
145	        };
146	
147	        let mut routes = Vec::new();
148	        let mut context_windows = BTreeMap::new();
149	        let mut context_window_sources = BTreeMap::new();
150	        for name in route_names {
151	            let Some(mut entry) = providers.remove(&name) else {
152	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
153	                    "unknown provider route {name}"
154	                )));
155	            };
156	            if let Some(model) = override_model {
157	                entry.model = Some(model.to_string());
158	            }
159	            let catalog_entry =
160	                apply_catalog_to_provider_entry(&name, &mut entry, registry, catalog_override);
161	            let context_window = catalog_entry.and_then(|entry| entry.context_window);
162	            let context_window_source = catalog_entry.and_then(|entry| {
163	                entry.context_window.map(|_| match entry.source {
164	                    CatalogEntrySource::Catalog => ModelContextWindowSource::Catalog,
165	                    CatalogEntrySource::Seam => ModelContextWindowSource::Seam,
166	                })
167	            });
168	            let kind = entry.kind.unwrap_or_else(|| kind_from_name(&name));
169	            entry.kind = Some(kind.clone());
170	            routes.push(build_provider(name.clone(), kind, entry, registry)?);
171	            context_windows.insert(name.clone(), context_window);
172	            context_window_sources.insert(name, context_window_source);
173	        }
174	
175	        Ok(Self {
176	            routes,
177	            context_windows,
178	            context_window_sources,
179	        })
180	    }

238	                failures.push(format!("{}: missing credential", route.name()));
239	                continue;
240	            }
241	            attempted += 1;
242	            match route.complete(request).await {
243	                Ok(response) => return Ok(response),
244	                Err(err) => {
245	                    failures.push(format!("{}: {err}", route.name()));
246	                    last_error = Some(err);
247	                }
248	            }
249	        }
250	        // A single attempted route surfaces its typed error so callers keep
251	        // the retryability signal (429/5xx/transport) instead of an opaque
252	        // NoRoute wrapper; multiple attempts mean fallthrough already
253	        // happened and the aggregate is final.
254	        if attempted == 1
255	            && let Some(err) = last_error
256	        {
257	            return Err(err);
258	        }
259	        Err(ProviderError::NoRoute(failures.join("; ")))
260	    }
261	
262	    pub fn estimate_for_route(
263	        &self,
264	        provider_name: Option<&str>,
265	        usage: ProviderUsage,
266	    ) -> Result<SpendEstimate> {
267	        let route = provider_name
268	            .and_then(|name| self.routes.iter().find(|route| route.name() == name))
269	            .or_else(|| self.routes.first())
270	            .ok_or_else(|| ProviderError::NoRoute("empty provider route".to_string()))?;
271	        Ok(route.estimate_spend(usage))
272	    }
273	}
274	
275	fn configured_route_names(
276	    default_provider: Option<String>,
277	    fallback: Option<Vec<String>>,
278	) -> Vec<String> {
279	    let mut route_names = Vec::new();
280	    if let Some(default_provider) = default_provider {
281	        route_names.push(default_provider);
282	    }
283	    if let Some(fallback) = fallback {
284	        for provider in fallback {
285	            if !route_names.iter().any(|route| route == &provider) {
286	                route_names.push(provider);
287	            }
288	        }
289	    }
290	    if route_names.is_empty() {
291	        route_names.extend([
292	            "cli:claude-code".to_string(),
293	            "cli:codex".to_string(),
294	            "anthropic".to_string(),
295	            "openai".to_string(),
296	            "openai-compatible".to_string(),
297	        ]);
298	    }
299	    route_names
300	}
301	
302	fn build_provider(
303	    name: String,
304	    kind: ProviderKind,
305	    entry: ProviderEntry,
306	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
307	) -> Result<Box<dyn Provider>> {
308	    match kind {
309	        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => Ok(Box::new(CliClaudeCodeProvider::new(name, entry))),
310	        ProviderKind::CliCodex => Ok(Box::new(CliCodexProvider::new(name, entry))),
311	        ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => Ok(Box::new(ScriptedSmokeProvider::new())),
312	        ProviderKind::Anthropic | ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
313	            Ok(Box::new(ProviderAdapter::new(name, kind, entry)))
314	        }
315	        ProviderKind::Generic(id) => {
316	            let descriptor = registry
317	                .get(&id)
318	                .or_else(|| registry.get(&name))
319	                .ok_or_else(|| {
320	                    ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("generic provider {id} has no descriptor"))
321	                })?;
322	            if descriptor.kind != DescriptorKind::Cli {
323	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
324	                    "generic provider {id} is not a cli descriptor"
325	                )));
326	            }
327	            Ok(Box::new(GenericCliProvider::new(
328	                name,
329	                entry,
330	                descriptor.clone(),
331	            )?))
332	        }
333	    }
334	}
335

932	fn should_cancel_run(state: &PipelineState, token: &CancellationToken) -> bool {
933	    state.status == RunStatus::Killed || token.is_cancelled() || cancel_marker_present(state)
934	}
935	
936	/// Backoff before the single transient-error retry: long enough for a rate
937	/// limit window to move, short enough to be negligible against a turn.
938	const PROVIDER_RETRY_BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
939	
940	/// Run a provider completion bounded by the remaining wall budget. `None`
941	/// means the budget elapsed first: the turn token is cancelled so the
942	/// provider subprocess is reaped, with a bounded grace period for cleanup
943	/// before the future is dropped.
944	async fn complete_within_wall_budget<F>(
945	    completion: F,
946	    wall_remaining: Option<Duration>,
947	    turn_token: &CancellationToken,
948	) -> Option<deadreckon_providers::Result<ProviderResponse>>
949	where
950	    F: std::future::Future<Output = deadreckon_providers::Result<ProviderResponse>>,
951	{
952	    tokio::pin!(completion);
953	    let Some(remaining) = wall_remaining else {
954	        return Some(completion.await);
955	    };
956	    if let Ok(result) = tokio::time::timeout(remaining, &mut completion).await {
957	        Some(result)
958	    } else {
959	        turn_token.cancel();
960	        let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), &mut completion).await;
961	        None
962	    }
963	}

966	    DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("provider error: {err}"))
967	}

973	struct CancelMarkerGuard {
974	    shutdown: CancellationToken,
975	    handle: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
976	}
977	
978	impl CancelMarkerGuard {
979	    fn spawn(run_root: &Path, run_token: CancellationToken) -> Self {
980	        let shutdown = CancellationToken::new();
981	        let shutdown_for_task = shutdown.clone();
982	        let marker = cancel_marker_path_for_run_root(run_root);
983	        let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
984	            loop {
985	                tokio::select! {
986	                    _ = shutdown_for_task.cancelled() => break,
987	                    _ = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)) => {
988	                        if marker.exists() {
989	                            run_token.cancel();
990	                            break;
991	                        }
992	                    }
993	                }
994	            }
995	        });
996	        Self { shutdown, handle }
997	    }
998	}
999	
1000	impl Drop for CancelMarkerGuard {
1001	    fn drop(&mut self) {
1002	        self.shutdown.cancel();
1003	        self.handle.abort();
1004	    }
1005	}

1007	// SAFETY: `RunLoopOutcome` is the stable event vocabulary used at call sites.
1008	#[allow(clippy::needless_pass_by_value)]
1009	fn emit_run_completed(
1010	    state: &PipelineState,
1011	    sender: Option<&broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
1012	    outcome: RunLoopOutcome,
1013	) -> Result<()> {
1014	    let status = match outcome {
1015	        RunLoopOutcome::Done => "completed",
1016	        RunLoopOutcome::PausedAtCap => "paused",
1017	        RunLoopOutcome::Killed => "killed",
1018	        RunLoopOutcome::Failed => "failed",
1019	    };
1020	    emit_event(
1021	        state,
1022	        sender,
1023	        RunEventKind::RunCompleted {
1024	            status: status.to_string(),
1025	        },
1026	    )
1027	}

1029	fn build_prompt(state: &PipelineState, history: &[String]) -> String {
1030	    let history_text = if history.is_empty() {
1031	        "none".to_string()
1032	    } else {
1033	        history.join("\n")
1034	    };
1035	    let spec_text = spec_prompt_text(state);
1036	    let skill_text = run_skill_text(state);
1037	    format!(
1038	        "You are deadreckon running unattended coding work.\nWorking directory: {}\nSPEC:\n{}\n\nSkill and implementation-notes contract:\n{}\n\nHistory:\n{}\n\nReturn exactly one JSON object with action bash, write_file, or done.",
1039	        state.working_dir.display(),
1040	        spec_text,
1041	        skill_text,
1042	        history_text
1043	    )
1044	}

Do not write outside it. Do not ask questions. When finished, print a concise summary of changed files.\nHistory:\n{}",
1056	        state.working_dir.display(),

1075	fn implementation_notes_contract() -> String {
1076	    format!(
1077	        "Implement the SPEC in the working directory.\n\nAs you work, maintain {IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML} at the working-directory root. Keep it current with anything the owner should know about how the implementation interprets or diverges from the spec:\n- Design decisions: choices made where the spec was ambiguous.\n- Deviations: intentional departures from the spec, with reasons.\n- Tradeoffs: alternatives considered and why the chosen path won.\n- Open questions: anything the owner should confirm or revise.\n\nBefore reporting done, update {IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES_HTML} after the latest documentable code/config/test/doc change. The run docs render the same content into RUN-DECISIONS.md, which is the published Markdown ledger."
1078	    )
1079	}

1081	fn acceptance_prompt_text(state: &PipelineState) -> String {
1082	    let yaml_path = acceptance_spec_path_for_run_root(&state.run_root);
1083	    let yaml = std::fs::read_to_string(&yaml_path).ok();
1084	    let markdown = std::fs::read_to_string(state.run_root.join("acceptance.md")).ok();
1085	    match (yaml, markdown) {
1086	        (Some(yaml), Some(markdown)) => format!(
1087	            "{}\n\nacceptance.yaml:\n{}",
1088	            markdown.trim(),
1089	            yaml.trim()
1090	        ),
1091	        (Some(yaml), None) => format!("acceptance.yaml:\n{}", yaml.trim()),
1092	        (None, _) => {
1093	            "default dr-gate behavior: working directory exists, or cargo test when Cargo.toml exists"
1094	                .to_string()
1095	        }
1096	    }
1097	}

1296	fn spawn_event_sink_forwarder(
1297	    seams: SeamsConfig,
1298	    ctx: SeamRunCtx,
1299	    sender: &broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>,
1300	) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> {
1301	    let mut receiver = sender.subscribe();
1302	    tokio::spawn(async move {
1303	        loop {
1304	            match receiver.recv().await {
1305	                Ok(event) => {
1306	                    let Ok(req) = serde_json::to_value(event) else {
1307	                        continue;
1308	                    };
1309	                    let _ = dispatch_seam(SeamKind::EventSink, &req, &seams, &ctx).await;
1310	                }
1311	                Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => continue,
1312	                Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => break,
1313	            }
1314	        }
1315	    })
1316	}

1454	fn load_or_reconstruct_history(
1455	    state: &mut PipelineState,
1456	    from_turn: Option<u32>,
1457	) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
1458	    let trace_reconstruction = reconstruct_history_from_traces(state)?;
1459	    let history_exists = history_path(state).exists();
1460	    let mut history = if history_exists {
1461	        load_history(state)?
1462	    } else {
1463	        trace_reconstruction.history
1464	    };
1465	    if let Some(from_turn) = from_turn {
1466	        history.truncate(from_turn as usize);
1467	        state.turn = from_turn;
1468	        truncate_run_artifacts_after_turn(state, from_turn)?;
1469	        save_history(state, &history)?;
1470	        save_state(state)?;
1471	    } else if !history_exists && trace_reconstruction.last_complete_turn > state.turn {
1472	        state.turn = trace_reconstruction.last_complete_turn;
1473	        save_history(state, &history)?;
1474	        save_state(state)?;
1475	    }
1476	    Ok(history)
1477	}

1482	}
1483	
1484	fn reconstruct_history_from_traces(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<ReconstructedHistory> {
1485	    let path = state.run_root.join("traces.jsonl");
1486	    if !path.exists() {
1487	        return Ok(ReconstructedHistory {
1488	            history: Vec::new(),
1489	            last_complete_turn: 0,
1490	        });
1491	    }
1492	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).with_path(&path)?;
1493	    let mut complete_lines = Vec::new();
1494	    let mut history = Vec::new();
1495	    let mut last_complete_turn = 0;
1496	    for line in raw.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
1497	        let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
1498	            break;
1499	        };
1500	        complete_lines.push(line.to_string());
1501	        let event = value
1502	            .get("event")
1503	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
1504	            .unwrap_or_default();
1505	        let turn = value
1506	            .get("turn")
1507	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
1508	            .unwrap_or_default() as u32;
1509	        if is_completed_tool_trace(event)
1510	            && let Some(tool_call_id) = value
1511	                .pointer("/detail/tool_call_id")
1512	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
1513	        {
1514	            history.push(format!(
1515	                "tool {tool_call_id} result: reconstructed from trace"
1516	            ));
1517	            last_complete_turn = last_complete_turn.max(turn);
1518	        }
1519	    }
1520	    let sanitized = complete_lines.join("\n");
1521	    if sanitized.len() != raw.trim_end_matches('\n').len() {
1522	        std::fs::write(
1523	            &path,
1524	            if sanitized.is_empty() {
1525	                String::new()
1526	            } else {
1527	                format!("{sanitized}\n")
1528	            },
1529	        )
1530	        .with_path(&path)?;
1531	    }
1532	    Ok(ReconstructedHistory {
1533	        history,
1534	        last_complete_turn,
1535	    })
1536	}
1537	
1538	fn is_completed_tool_trace(event: &str) -> bool {
1539	    matches!(event, "tool.bash" | "tool.write_file" | "tool.cli_subagent")
1540	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-09 19:23:33Z)**_

Looking at the diff and reading the actual files, I've traced each change. Key observations:

1. `error.rs` — added `retryable: bool` field; CLI retryability is now a case-insensitive substring match against a hardcoded marker list. Logic-level concern (false positives if a non-retryable CLI failure happens to embed one of those phrases in stderr) but capped at one retry — not security-impactful.

2. `http.rs` — new client with connect/total timeouts, but the build result has a `.unwrap_or_else(|_| reqwest::Client::new())` fallback. This is the one place where the diff silently undoes its own safety control. See finding below.

3. `http.rs` — `trim_for_error` char-boundary fix is correct (0 is always a boundary so the `unwrap_or(0)` floor is safe).

4. `router.rs` — single-attempt typed-error pass-through is intentional and properly bounded (it only changes whether the inner typed error or a wrapped `NoRoute` reaches the caller). No injection/leak path opened.

5. `turn_loop.rs` — the new one-shot retry guards on `is_retryable()` and `!should_cancel_run`. Wall budget recalc subtracts elapsed and clamps with `.max(1.0)` before `Duration::from_secs_f64`, so no panic/underflow. The new `state.failure_reason = format!("provider error: {err}")` persistence echoes provider error detail (≤240 chars of response body) to state.json — same content was already in the failures vec / events stream, so net new exposure is marginal and content is bounded; not a security regression worth filing on its own.

6. Tests files — not enforcement paths; nothing to flag.

The one defensive-coding finding worth recording:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-09 19:23:51Z)**_

I filed one low-severity finding: in `http.rs`, the new bounded-timeout client falls back to `reqwest::Client::new()` (no timeouts) on builder error — silently negating the very safety property the surrounding comment claims ("a stalled connection must never hang an unattended run"). The fallback should either propagate the error or preserve the timeouts.

No other security-impacting issues in the diff:
- CLI retryability substring matching is bounded to one retry, so even a false positive caps amplification at 2×.
- Router single-attempt typed-error pass-through doesn't expose new content (failure detail was already aggregated into `NoRoute`).
- Wall-budget recalc is clamped (`.max(1.0)`) before `Duration::from_secs_f64`, so no underflow/panic.
- `trim_for_error` char-boundary fix is correct (0 is always a boundary, so `unwrap_or(0)` is safe).
- New `state.failure_reason` persistence echoes provider error detail that was already in the events stream — marginal exposure increase, body trimmed to 240 chars.
